senses.definition: Essential or central; of great importance or relevance.
examples: He was instrumental in conducting the business.

quotes.text: The head is not more native to the heart, The hand more instrumental to the mouth
quotes.reference: c. 1599–1602 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Hamlet, Prince of Denmarke”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene ii]:

quotes.text: Few songwriters have been as instrumental in creating the mold for American music.
quotes.reference: 2012, Christoper Zara, Tortured Artists: From Picasso and Monroe to Warhol and Winehouse, the Twisted Secrets of the World's Most Creative Minds, part 1, chapter 2, 51:

quotes.text: [...] Prosser was instrumental in the decision in 2010 to recommence publication of an annual health and safety report, following a period when it had fallen into abeyance.
quotes.reference: 2020 July 29, Ian Prosser discusses with Paul Stephen, “Rail needs robust and strategic plans”, in Rail, page 40:

senses.definition: Serving as an instrument, medium, means, or agency.

quotes.text: Maxwell started back to his study, feeling that kind of satisfaction which a man feels when he has been even partly instrumental in finding an unemployed person a remunerative position.
quotes.reference: 1896, Charles M. Sheldon, chapter 12, in In His Steps:

senses.definition: (music) Pertaining to, made by, or prepared for an instrument, especially a musical instrument (rather than the human voice).

quotes.text: Sweet voices mix'd with instrumental sounds.
quotes.reference: c. 1700, John Dryden, Cymon and Iphigenia:

quotes.text: He defended the use of instrumental music in public worship.
quotes.reference: 1849–1861, Thomas Babington Macaulay, The History of England from the Accession of James the Second, volume (please specify |volume=I to V), London: Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, →OCLC:

senses.definition: (grammar) Applied to a case expressing means or agency, generally corresponding to the English use of prepositions such as by, with, through, or by means of with the objective case.
(music) A composition written or performed without lyrics or singing, using a lead instrument to replace vocals.

quotes.text: I recommend this album in the face of the fact that five of the eleven songs are the purest filler, dull instrumentals with a harmonica rifling over an indifferent rhythm section. The rest is magnificent […]

senses.definition: (music) A pause in the vocals of a song, usually occurring midway through, in which a musical instrument replaces the vocals.
